children: India TV Chairman and Editor-in-Chief Rajat Sharma has been unanimously re-elected President of the News Broadcasters and Digital Association (NBDA) for 2026-27.

The decision was taken at a meeting of the NBDA Board of Directors. The association’s other office-bearers will continue in their respective positions, with M.V. Shreyams Kumar, Managing Director, Mathrubhumi Printing & Publishing, retaining his position as Vice-President, and Anuradha Prasad Shukla, Chairperson and Managing Director, News24 Broadcast India, continuing as Honorary Treasurer.
Sharma, one of India’s prominent television journalists, began his career in journalism before launching his flagship interview programme
in 1993. He co-founded India TV with Ritu Dhawan in 2004 and has since led the channel as its Chairman and Editor-in-Chief.

Shreyams Kumar heads Mathrubhumi Printing & Publishing and its wider media operations, with experience across the group’s print, television and digital businesses. Prasad Shukla leads News24 Broadcast India and has held senior leadership positions across the news broadcasting industry.

Jayant Mammen Mathew, representing MM TV, is also part of the NBDA Board. He was appointed to the board at the association’s 19th Annual General Meeting and has experience across journalism and media management. MM TV operates Manorama News.

Meanwhile, Rachna Burman, Director, Public Policy & Content Assurance, The Times Group, and Kshipra Jatana, Group General Counsel, Network18 Media & Investments, have been appointed as Permanent Directors.

Other members of the NBDA Board include Kalli Purie Bhandal, Vice-Chairperson and Managing Director, TV Today Network; Anil Kumar Malhotra, Advisor, Zee Media Corporation; Dhruba Mukherjee, Director, ABP Network; Rahul Kanwal, CEO and Editor-in-Chief, NDTV; and Mahesh Kumar Rajaraman, Managing Director, Sun TV Network.
The NBDA currently has 29 news and current affairs broadcasters as members, representing 136 news channels and digital platforms.
